Create today's Chinese AI-curated technology trend report for this repository.

1. Use the `REPORT_DATE`, `REPORT_WINDOW_END`, and `GITHUB_TRENDING_ARG` environment variables prepared by the workflow. The report covers the exact 24-hour China Standard Time window ending at 07:00 on `REPORT_DATE` (for example, 2026-09-03 covers 2026-09-02 07:00 through 2026-09-03 07:00). Run `python outputs/tech_trend_report.py --window-end "$REPORT_WINDOW_END" $GITHUB_TRENDING_ARG --output outputs/tech-trends-raw.html --candidates-output outputs/tech-trend-candidates.json`. The raw preview is evidence only and must never be published as the final report.
2. Read `outputs/tech-trend-candidates.json`. It is evidence, not a final report. When `GITHUB_TRENDING_ARG` is present, use the first 10 repositories from both GitHub Trending Daily views: all languages and Chinese spoken language. The two lists are only candidate pools; deduplicate them and select projects for technical substance, not rank alone. When it is empty, this is a historical backfill: GitHub Trending has no dated archive, so do not use current Trending repositories or claim historical GitHub popularity.
3. Read every existing report for the previous seven report dates under `outputs/tech-trends-YYYY-MM-DD.html`. Do not repeat an item whose normalized primary URL, GitHub owner/repository, or underlying topic already appeared, unless there is a substantive new event. For any repeat, explain what materially changed and link the new primary evidence.
4. Select exactly 10 substantive items whenever 10 readable, technically meaningful candidates remain after deduplication. On a current-day report with GitHub Trending candidates, include at least 4 distinct `project_trending` repositories in the 10 items. Reserve these slots before filling the remainder with official releases or discussions. Only include fewer than 4 when fewer than 4 technically meaningful Trending repositories remain readable after the 7-day deduplication; state that shortfall and its reason explicitly. Read each selected primary URL before writing; omit inaccessible sources rather than guessing. Prioritize technical substance, official releases, independently corroborated discussion, GitHub Trending attention, and engineering impact. When fewer than 10 candidates can be verified, state the shortfall explicitly.
5. Write `outputs/tech-trends-REPORT_DATE.html` using the exact `REPORT_DATE` value. Use `Tech Morning Brief` as the English page title, and make the visible heading clear that this is a morning brief covering the preceding 24 hours through 07:00 China Standard Time. Include a Chinese editorial overview and, for each item: what happened, core technical point, why it matters, evidence/source links, and a maturity or risk note. Use a brief "值得继续观察" section for weaker early signals when useful. The total number of main and early-signal items should be exactly 10 whenever possible.
6. Update `outputs/tech-trends.html` as a lightweight HTML redirect/link to today's dated report, then run `python outputs/build_index.py` to refresh `index.html`.
7. Publish only `index.html`, `outputs/tech-trends.html`, and the new dated report. Stage only those files. Commit only when there is a change, using a concise date-specific message and a separate final commit-message line exactly `Agent: codex`, then push to `main`. Do not commit the raw preview, candidates JSON, or any workflow/prompt file.
8. In the final response, report source or publication failures and the path of the generated report.
